forms.label: Choose the bread
forms.japanese: 全粒粉パンでお願いします
forms.explanation: 全粒粉パン is the noun "whole-wheat bread." で marks the option being chosen, and お願いします is a polite phrase meaning "I would like (this), please."

forms.label: Ask for toasting
forms.japanese: パンを焼いてもらえますか
forms.explanation: パンを is the object of 焼く (to toast). 焼いて is the te-form of 焼く. もらえますか is the potential form of もらう (to receive) in a question, so 〜てもらえますか asks whether someone can do something for you.

forms.label: Ask to change an ingredient
forms.japanese: チーズを変更できますか
forms.explanation: チーズを marks the thing being changed as the object. 変更できます is the potential form of 変更する (to change), meaning "can change," and か turns it into a polite question.

speakingObjectives: Choose whole-wheat bread and a chicken filling when the shop staff asks which bread and filling you want.
Ask for lettuce and tomato to be added and for less mayonnaise, using 〜を入れてください and 〜は少なめでお願いします.
Ask for the bread to be toasted, say no onion, and ask whether the cheese can be changed to another one.

forms.label: Ask what is in it
forms.explanation: 何 is the question word "what," marked as the subject with が. 入っています is the te-form 入って plus います, describing the state of something being contained. か makes the sentence a question.

forms.label: Ask how it is made
forms.japanese: どうやって作りますか
forms.explanation: どうやって asks "by what method." 作ります is the polite form of 作る (to make or prepare), and か makes it a question.

forms.label: Ask if it is still available
forms.explanation: まだ means "still." ありますか is the polite form of ある (to exist or be available) in a question. Things are described with ある.

speakingObjectives: Listen as the server names today's daily set meal, then ask what it contains.
Ask what the set meal contains and how the chicken is prepared, using 何が入っていますか and どうやって作りますか.
Ask whether the set meal is still available and how much it costs, then ask whether it can be ready quickly.
Order the set meal to go with 持ち帰りでお願いします after checking the time it will take.

forms.label: Ask which one is recommended
forms.japanese: うどんと鶏肉の丼では、どちらがおすすめですか
forms.english: Which do you recommend, the udon or the chicken rice bowl?
forms.explanation: うどんと鶏肉の丼 joins the two options with と. では sets the scope of the comparison. どちら asks 'which of the two' and が marks it as the subject; おすすめです means 'is the recommended one,' and か makes it a question.

forms.label: Ask about the difference
forms.japanese: 二つの違いは何ですか
forms.english: What is the difference between the two?
forms.explanation: 二つ means "two things." の links it to 違い (difference), so 二つの違い means "the difference between the two." は marks the topic, 何 is the question word "what," and ですか makes the sentence a polite question.

forms.label: Ask about portion size
forms.explanation: 量 (amount, portion) is the topic, marked by は. 多い is an i-adjective meaning 'a lot' or 'much'; with 量, it asks whether the portion is large. ですか makes the question polite.

speakingObjectives: Ask the server which of the udon or the chicken rice bowl they recommend, and ask what the difference between the two is.
Ask whether the rice bowl portion is large and whether its sauce is spicy before choosing.
Ask whether the udon is a local dish, then confirm there is soup and choose the udon.
